A field demonstration could proceed by completing parameter tuning based on existing EMT results, executing the commissioning workflows for GFM BESS and GFM wind, and verifying response behavior using the already-installed high-speed data acquisition system. These steps provide the most direct path to evaluating GFM performance under real grid disturbances. Execute System-Level Disturbance Demonstration With permanent measurement equipment installed and configured during BP1, natural or planned system disturbances can be used to assess angle-support behavior, fast active-power injection, voltage-forming dynamics, protection interactions, and mixed GFM/GFL coordination. These events would yield essential validation data for EMT and positive-sequence models and would reduce uncertainty in future deployments. Validate GFM Performance Metrics in Field Conditions The performance metrics established in Task 1 can be validated using synchronized field measurements. Field-based evaluation would enable refinement of acceptable performance ranges, verification methods, and application guidance, supporting their future use in utility planning, interconnection studies, and model validation efforts. 9.2 Future Modeling and Simulation Development Complete Positive-Sequence GFM Model Development Early work completed during BP1, including model structure concepts and preliminary parameter definitions, provides the foundation for a full positive- sequence model for GFM Type-3 wind turbines. Future development would focus on completing model equations for virtual inertia, angle regulation, voltage-forming behavior, mode transitions, and protection interactions; parameterizing the model using EMT and field data; and validating performance using the high-speed measurement infrastructure. Improve EMT-Positive Sequence Coordination A key area for continued development is aligning EMT and positive-sequence representations of GFM behavior, particularly for angle stiffness, damping, DC-link dynamics, and current-limited conditions. Enhancing cross-model consistency will improve the accuracy of interconnection-level studies and support the broader use of GFM models in planning tools. Expand HIL Validation and Controller Tuning The real-time HIL platform built in BP1 provides a unique opportunity to test controller tuning strategies, evaluate protection schemes, and examine multi- resource coordination under realistic dynamic conditions. Future work could incorporate additional plant-level control functions, model-based timing constraints, and expanded system-disturbance scenarios. Page 27 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric 9.3 Future Data Analysis and Measurement Applications Develop a Field Data Analysis Framework With the measurement hardware fully installed, future work should focus on establishing automated tools for event detection, time-synchronized waveform processing, and comparison of field measurements with EMT and positive-sequence simulations. These tools would enable systematic model calibration and provide insight into GFM behavior across a range of operating conditions. Validate GFM Performance Across Operating Regimes Measurement-based evaluation across different grid strengths, dispatch conditions, and disturbance types will support refinement of controller parameters, improve reliability assessments, and establish evidence-based benchmarks for future GFM deployments. 9.4 Reducing Remaining Technical Risks Although BP1 delivered substantial progress, several areas will require additional work to fully mitigate technical risk: • GFM performance has not yet been validated under real weak-grid conditions.
